newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FedEx hopeful of Japan-U.S. air cargo deal.
newsitem.headline: FedEx hopeful of Japan-U.S. air cargo deal.

text.p: Federal Express Corp (FedEx) said on Wednesday it was optimistic that a meeting of U.S. and Japanese trade officials next week would bring a resolution to a dispute over air cargo rights a step closer.
"We're optimistic they will (when) they go back to the table next week," Michael Ducker, senior vice president of FedEx Asia Pacific told a news conference.
The dispute centres on so-called beyond rights, the right to fly to a third country from Japan, particularly China.
"We want them to get it sorted out so that FedEx can enjoy the best aviation rights that are possible," Ducker said.
FedEx wants a resolution, but Ducker said the dispute was "in no way impacting our ability to offer our services" to Asian clients.

FedEx has double digit growth in Asia with intra-Asia cargo its fastest expanding market globally, South Pacific vice president David Cunningham told reporters at the launch of two new Asian routes into and via the United States.
Negotiators for the two countries agreed earlier this month to strike a deal by the end of September, but U.S. officials have insisted the FedEx dispute be given priority treatment.
Japanese officials are concerned that U.S. pressure will lead only to U.S. domination of the air cargo business.
"We believe that a greater liberalisation of the market place provides greater advantages for Japanese manufacturers and consumers and that has always been our position," Drucker said.
